description: Codewhale through its NSIS setup and its winget package on Windows, installed and not run.
why: Codewhale has three witnesses here: the key its NSIS setup writes, the key winget writes for its portable package, and the setup's uninstaller, the one file of either install at the depth the per-user app branch reads. require_rows holds each, the setup's key by the end of its registry path because winget's key contains its name, so removing one value leaves the others to find it. forbid_rows holds npm's package and ~\.codewhale absent, so neither a third route nor a first run is what finds it. deepseek-harness is forbidden because Codewhale started as deepseek-tui, opera-neon because its launcher is read by the same per-user app branch, and cursor because its Uninstall key is read by the same branch.
known_gaps: winget's package is portable: its files are under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WinGet, which no Windows branch reads, so its Uninstall key is its only witness.
